title: DEIM-M vs RT-DETR-R34: benchmark on the same protocol
dek: Measured on the same COCO protocol: DEIM-M leads by 3.3 mAP points with fewer parameters, but RT-DETR-R34 is 29.41% faster on desktop GPU.
author: Vision Analysis

blocks.text: DEIM-M is the more accurate model: 55.5 vs 52.2 mAP@50-95 against RT-DETR-R34 on an RTX 5070 Ti in PyTorch, and it reaches that with fewer parameters (19.59M vs 31.44M) and less VRAM (189 vs 213 MB). RT-DETR-R34 is the faster detector on that GPU: 40.2 vs 28.4 FPS, a 29.41% edge. On Raspberry Pi 5 the speed gap disappears. Pick by deployment target.

DEIM-M (19.59M parameters, Apache-2.0) and RT-DETR-R34 (31.44M, Apache-2.0) both evaluate at 640 px input, so the input resolution matches and does not skew the comparison. DEIM-M is the smaller model here. Both have verified rows on desktop GPU, Jetson Orin, and Raspberry Pi 5, so this comparison covers the deploy targets where the answer changes.

blocks.caption: Accuracy vs parameters on COCO val2017. DEIM-M and RT-DETR-R34 highlighted against the full set.

blocks.text: mAP is shown in percent form. DEIM-M measures 55.5 mAP@50-95 to RT-DETR-R34's 52.2, a 3.3 point lead. The gap is wider on small objects: 39.1 vs 34.9 mAP_small, an 11.77% relative difference. DEIM-M reaches that accuracy with fewer parameters than RT-DETR-R34.
On the RTX 5070 Ti, RT-DETR-R34 runs 40.2 FPS to DEIM-M's 28.4 in PyTorch, a 29.41% edge. The gap holds under conversion: 77.7 vs 57.6 FPS on ONNX Runtime, 98.1 vs 85.4 FPS on TensorRT FP32.
The speed verdict does not travel to CPU. On Raspberry Pi 5 both models run 0.6 FPS, so the desktop gap disappears there. On Jetson Orin RT-DETR-R34 keeps its edge: 8.0 vs 7.0 FPS.

Pick DEIM-M when accuracy or memory matters, or when the target is a Raspberry Pi where the speed gap closes: it is more accurate at every object size and uses less VRAM. Pick RT-DETR-R34 for desktop, server, or Jetson GPU throughput, where it leads on every GPU runtime measured. Both ship under Apache-2.0, so licensing does not force the choice.

# pip install libreyolo
from libreyolo import LibreYOLO

deim = LibreYOLO("LibreDEIMm.pt")        # 19.59M params, 55.5 mAP@50-95
rtdetr = LibreYOLO("LibreRTDETRr34.pt")  # 31.44M params, 52.2 mAP@50-95

results = deim("image.jpg")
